content.summary_of_the_paper: This work studies different masking methods for machine unlearning. The authors claim the masking based on approximated Fisher score performs the best. The authors also study different noisy ratios and learning rate schedules.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The paper is clearly organized and easy to follow.
2. The authors provide intensive experiments.

Weakness:
1. I hope the author could elaborate more on the broader impact of machine unlearning. Currently, this paper seems benchmarking different masking methods on toy datasets and standard models, which makes the scope of this work quite limited.
2. Could you elaborate more on the relationship between machine unlearning vs. differential privacy? I think the latter also aims to remove some data instead of a whole class which is too aggressive. It is also important to show if the proposed masking method is better than differential privacy methods.
3. Results in Tables 1 and 2: I suppose the variance should also be included.
4. I did not see any more ablation studies on the size of the removed group of samples except the Figure 4. I think it is important to compare methods under different removed group sizes.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Overall this work is clearly organized, with high-quality experiments.
However, the scope and impact of this work seem limited, due to the lack of connection to real-life cases and related works.
content.summary_of_the_review:
In general, I think this paper is well-written, but the novelty and impact may be limited.
I hope the authors could address my concerns mentioned above.

content.title: Response to Reviewer yX3y
content.comment:
Thanks for your valuable comments. We address many questions in our general response, and here are the specific responses.  

- about the impact of machine unlearning
  - As the amount of data grows exponentially, models become bigger and bigger, and so does the concern about leakage of data privacy. Recently, legal laws such as General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) are proposed to declare that consumers have the right to ask business companies to remove their data. And the companies are required to not use their privacy data any more, more importantly, delete their user data on the existing model. 
  - The same situation also occurs in when we need to remove some outliers from training set, such as noisy data, systematic biases or poisoned data for backdoor attack. In these settings, an effective way to unlearn some observed training data for various models is quite necessary.
  
- about relationship between machine unlearning vs. differential privacy
  - Differential privacy is another related task, and it focuses on guaranteeing that information about training data could not be leaked by the trained model. It requires the model to remain unchanged after replacing any one of the training data. And machine unlearning could be viewed as a generalization of differential privacy when removing one data point according to definition. Previous studies try to add noise on gradient during learning to hide the data information, which will inevitably degrade model performance and could not be applied for scenarios with high accuracy requirements, such as face recognition and financial risk measurement.
  - Compared to machine unlearning, differential privacy is a much stronger condition because it asks the model do not leak information about any particular individual training samples. Differential privacy is a sufficient condition for instance removal, while the model under differential privacy often suffer a significant loss in accuracy even for a loose privacy constraint.
  
- about the variance in Tables 1 and 2
  - We will add the variance in table 1 and 2, thanks for your suggestions.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a new way to remove specific information from a trained model. The proposed method first tries to identify important parameters that are relevant to the content to be erased, and then performs a fine-tuning on the unmasked parameters with the remaining dataset. The new strategy is applied to various datasets including CIFAR10, MNIST, and Tinyimagenet. The experimental results show that the proposed method performs better; it can maintain the performance on the remaining data while forgetting the target data.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
- The technical details of the paper are easy to follow.
- The experiments are conducted with various datasets to show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Weaknesses

- The motivation for unlearning an entire class is unclear to me. If one wants to remove the entire class, why not remove the final softmax unit corresponding to the target class? It will also achieve zero accuracies without affecting the performances of the other classes.
- The assumption that the entire remaining dataset (D_r) is accessible seems quite strong to me since due to the privacy issue, one may not keep the entire dataset used for training.
- About the experiments with limited remaining data, there are several methods proposed to unlearn without accessing the remaining dataset. Please add a comparison with the previous methods.
- How does w^*_r is obtained in Figure 1? and why is it different from the Retrain curve? "takes a long time to learn" does not explain the gap between these two curves in Figure 1. For example, their difference with the Tinyimagenet on the Densenet is more than 10%, and the "Retrain" model does not reach the red-dashed line guessed from the learning curve. Are they obtained from different learning algorithms? or if not how many epochs do you need to get the red-dashed line?
- The outlier detection experiments assume the existence of noisy data. Learning with noisy labels is also well-studied and does not require an unlearning process. It would be good to have a comparison with these approaches.
- The figures are difficult to read. Please make the lines more readable.
- Please report the performance of the original model without noise in Table 2.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well-written and easy to follow. The use of Fisher information to identify the important parameters is not very new. Thus the novelty of the work is somewhat limited. I haven't checked the details of the supplementary materials, but I haven't found any issues with reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: Although the proposed method empirically performs well given the experimental setting, the motivation of the experiment is somewhat unclear and the technical novelty is somewhat limited.

content.title: Response to Reviewer pwYb
content.comment:
Thanks for your valuable comments. We address many questions in our general response, and here are the specific responses.  

- about "the assumption of the entire remaining dataset (D_r) is accessible"
  * We show the results of accessing the entire remaining dataset in Figure 2. Besides that, to relax that condition, we also explore several relaxed scenarios.  
  * One scenario is that we do not save the original remain data, avoiding privacy leakage problems, and we only save some intermediate values (activation values) for remaining data. In this way, we could only mask some neurons based our method (without fine-tuning). The results (in Table 1) show that our method could maintains 87% of its original performance while almost forgot completely. 
  * To consider a stronger privacy restrictions, we consider another two scenarios where there are no remaining data or only 0.1% remaining data. We use the limited 0.1% remaining data both in masking and fine-tuning steps. The results (in Figure 3) show that when no remaining data is accessible, our method could unlearn completely and have a highest remain accuracy among other methods. When limited remaining data is accessible, accuracy on remain data could be largely boosted.

* about curves on Figure 2
  * The w^*_r (retrained model) in Figure 2 is the model we retrained from scratch without the forget samples.  The retrained model are trained for the same epochs as the original model (e.g., 160 epochs for cifar10/100), the detailed training statistics are showed in Appendix B. The red horizontal dashed line indicates the final performance of retrained model and red curve indicates the accuracy changes from the beginning. Some curves do not reach the horizontal line because we only fine-tune unlearned model for few epochs, it takes a long time for retrained model to achieve the final performance.

* about the performance of the original model without noise in table 2
  * The performance of the original model without noise could be found in Figure 2 at epoch 0. We will add the numbers in the title of table 2 for the convenience of reading. Thanks for your suggestions.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposed a new masking strategy based on Fisher information for model unlearning tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:
1. Under a linear model, the authors presented that the distance between the well-trained model on the entire dataset and the masked model is upper bounded by the Fisher information based term, which provided the evidence of the masking strategy. 
2. The proposed masking strategy is demonstrated more effective than other baselines over Forget Acc and Remain Acc.

Cons:
1. I think the authors have misunderstood the model unlearning task, which had caused a meaningless motivation (Fig. 1). “Forget” in model unlearning is not letting the tuned learned model have the lowest accuracy on removed samples but aims to obtain a model which is trained as if it has never seen the removed samples. For example, a well-trained SVM has a few support vectors. If only one of the support vectors needs removing, the SVM will not necessarily modify, and its prediction on the removed sample is still correct. More specifically, if the authors agree to my understanding to machine unlearning, Finetuning on remaining samples should be the golden standard as it is used in influence-based unlearning research. If authors insist the definition of "forget" should be low accuracy on removed samples, another branch of related works is absent in this paper, that is, model editing [1]. 
2. The challenge of escaping the local minimum cannot be directly derived from the motivation figure, though it might be true. I would like to say it is a conjecture.
3. I think the amount of removed samples matters in this problem. Most previous works for unlearning are focusing on removing a small number of samples, e.g., outliers. Accelerating the unlearning via parameters masking/selection is restrictedly helpful when many samples are to be removed.
4. Following 3, Fisher information has been used in other model tuning tasks [2] to select parameters. The only difference is that [2] is cross-domain and the proposed is from a whole set to a subset. However, such research has not been discussed in this paper.
5. "One-step Newton update" on page 1 misrefers to Graves et al. Please check it.

[1] EDITABLE NEURAL NETWORKS, ICLR 2020
[2] Few-shot Image Generation with Elastic Weight Consolidation, Neurips 2020.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This work could be better if it carefully clarifies the targeted problem. The technique novelty is not enough from my view.
content.summary_of_the_review: Unlearning is an interesting task. Be careful there is another related research direction that crafts unlearnable examples. Although authors can redefine the meaning of unlearning, the paper should be consistent with itself and the literature as well. I agree that FisheMasking is efficient if one wants to remove many examples. I sincerely hope my comments can help the authors improve this work.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.title: Response to Reviewer Bz8Q
content.comment:
Thanks for your valuable comments. We address most questions in our general response, and here are the specific responses.  

- about "fisher information used in other model tuning tasks"
  * Using Fisher Information to identify important weight are investigated in many research, but we would like to argue that we are the first to use fisher information to mask neurons for unlearning. Various experiments shows the effectiveness of our methods. 
  * We cite the EWC work [1] which first use fisher information to select important weight in continual learning. Their work focus on overcoming forgetting in continual learning while our paper focus on the opposite direction, accelerate forgetting in machine unlearning.

[1] Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks. James Kirkpatrick, Razvan Pascanu, Neil Rabinowitz, Joel Veness, Guillaume Desjardins, Andrei A Rusu, Kieran Milan, John Quan, Tiago Ramalho, Agnieszka Grabska-Barwinska, et al. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2017.

content.title: Response to all reviewers
content.comment:
We  thank all the reviewers for their valuable suggestions and comments. We are encouraged to hear from the reviewers found the machine unlearning task we investigated is interesting (*Reviewer Bz8Q*) and all the reviewers agree that our fisher-masking unlearning strategies is helpful ( *Reviewer Bz8Q*), effective (*Reviewer pwYb*) and high-quality (*Reviewer yX3y*). We also notice that  most of the questions are focused on the motivation and experiment settings.  We provide a general response to all reviewers to answer these common questions, individual responses blow to address each reviewer's concern, and a revised manuscript based on reviewers' comments.

- about machine unlearning and target model
  * We would like to point out that we think the machine unlearning task "aims to obtain a model which is trained as if it has never seen the removed samples" rather than "have the lowest accuracy on removed samples" (agree with *Reviewer Bz8Q* ). 
  * In this context, the golden standard model in all unlearning experiment should be the retrained model rather than the model fine-tuning on the remain samples. Direct fine-tuning could not unlearn the whole category which we illustrated in our experiments and it means the fine-tuning model can not act as if it has never seen the removed samples.  Although some influenced-based unlearning research often use the fine-tuning model as the target model, we do not believe that is the best option. 

- about the motivation and experiment settings (why we use "unlearning a whole class" as the main experiment setting)
  - The evaluation of machine unlearning is very difficult, especially on random group. Due to the fact that there are usually many copies of each data in the dataset, the retrained model after removing a random group could be identical to the original model. Thus most unlearning methods often experiment on removing a whole category and test the unlearned model on forget samples [1-3]. In this way, the unlearned model should act as the retrained model, and has zero accuracy on the forget samples (we do not think "forget" means "have the lowest accuracy on removed samples", but in category unlearn experiment, it is true). 
  - It is also true that in category unlearning experiment, "remove the final softmax unit corresponding to the target class" could be effective. But the information about the target class inside the model could not be scrubbed (in all our masking strategies, we do not modify the last classification layer). The information inside the models could be leaked if the attacker somehow obtain the intermediate representations and apply attacking methods, such as membership inference attack methods (Appendix C includes the experiment on readout functions,  such as membership inference attack). 

- about the group of removing samples
  - Although the main experiment setting in our paper is unlearning a whole class, removing a random group is also feasible. We use a outlier deletion experiment to show the effectiveness of our method on random group deletion. Table 2 shows the results when the group size of removing samples varies from 10% to 50%.


Regarding feedback from Reviewers Bz8Q, pwYb, and yX3y of our manuscript, we update our manuscript including the following changes.
* fix misreference of "One-step Newton update" on page 1 according to Reviewer Bz8Q.
* add performance of the original model in table 2 according to Reviewer pwYb.
* add variance in table 1 and table 2 according to Reviewer yX3y.

**References**

[1] Eternal sunshine of the spotless net: Selective forgetting in deep networks. Aditya Golatkar, Alessandro Achille, and Stefano Soatto. In 2020 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, CVPR 2020. 

[2] Forgetting outside the box: Scrubbing deep networks of information accessible from input-output observations. Aditya Golatkar, Alessandro Achille, and Stefano Soatto, Computer Vision - ECCV 2020 - 16th European Conference.

[3] Federated unlearning via class-discriminative pruning.  Junxiao Wang, Song Guo, Xin Xie, and Heng Qi. In WWW ’22: The ACM Web Conference 2022.
